messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: kv-cache autoscale alarm triggered on prod-gpu-pool-7, memory pressure > 85% across nodes, error-rate spike on continuous-batching path. Auto-notification to #incidents and oncall.
casey_oncall: acknowledging. grabbing logs and looking at nodes. @maria_g @jordan_r you free?
maria_g: I can join. pulling top keys and draft/target metrics now.
jordan_r: joining — looks like speculative-decoding is producing a lot of transient drafts that are being inserted into KV with long TTLs, causing cache blowup and larger batches.
sam_ops: seeing sudden batch_size jump from ~8-> ~48 on several workers, leads to CPU/GPU contention and tail latency cliffs.
casey_oncall: initial impact: 6 customer-facing routes show 95p latency > 2s, error 5xx up from 0.2%->1.8%. No full outages yet.
eli_support: PSR opened with customer X (tenant id t-129) reporting timeouts. Notifying their CSM.
maria_g: extracted KVC stats: insert_rate spiked x12, average entry size up 3x (draft objects storing full token arrays). TTLs incorrectly set to 60m for draft entries due to config regression.
jordan_r: config change summary: speculative-decoding change rolled last deploy removed draft TTL override; combined with continuous-batching change to prefer draft caching. So drafts are persisting.
casey_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) reduce speculative-decoding concurrency on prod-gpu-pool-7 2) temporarily set draft TTL to 30s 3) force eviction policy to LRU aggressive 4) throttle ingress to affected routes. Who can execute each?
sam_ops: I can push TTL + eviction flags and throttle ingress via ingress-proxy. Running:
```
# set draft TTL to 30s
kubectl -n infra exec configmapctl -- /bin/sh -c "update-config kvcache.speculativeDraftTTL=30"
# set eviction to aggressive
kubectl -n infra exec configmapctl -- /bin/sh -c "update-config kvcache.evictionPolicy=aggressive"
# scale down speculative concurrency
kubectl -n models set env deploy/spec-decode DEP_SPEC_CONCURRENCY=2 --record
```
ops-bot: Command received: updating config. Applying changes to 8 nodes.
ops-bot: Config update success: kvcache.speculativeDraftTTL=30, kvcache.evictionPolicy=aggressive.
casey_oncall: throttling ingress for route /v1/chat/stream for tenants t-100..t-150 to 30rps. Doing canary in us-west-2 first.
sam_ops: canary applied to us-west-2, route throttle: 30rps. Observing metrics for 2 min.
maria_g: glance at batch sizes — median drops from 32->9 in canary within 90s. Good sign.
jordan_r: still seeing high KV insert churn in eu-west-1, will apply same config there.
casey_oncall: customer impact update: reduced p95 from 2.2s->0.9s for canary customers. Errors down to baseline. Notifying CSM for a status update.
eli_support: CSM confirms customer X is aware and awaiting ETA.
devex-liz: reflagging eval harness — we need a regression test that ensures speculative draft TTLs cannot be unset. Filing followup ticket.
maria_g: doing deeper analysis — draft vs target keys are colliding because the key prefixing logic changed in the same deploy, causing sync mismatches and increased key churn. Root cause likely two independent PRs touching kv key namespace + speculative TTL default.
jordan_r: plan for next 30m: 1) propagate TTL+eviction to all regions 2) rollback key-prefix change on staging then prod if regression confirmed 3) disable speculative draft caching flag until we have guardrails.
casey_oncall: agree. @sam_ops please propagate to eu & asia. @jordan_r coordinate the rollback PR. @maria_g collect a short RCA timeline for post-incident.
sam_ops: propagating now to eu-west-1 and ap-northeast-1.
ops-bot: eu-west-1 changes applied. ap-northeast-1 changes applied.
maria_g: monitoring: global insert rate trending down, mem pressure dropping 85%->47% over 12 minutes. Batch sizes stabilizing.
casey_oncall: good. starting handoff notes for next oncall in 20m. Key things: root cause = speculative drafts persisted due to TTL unset + key-prefix change -> cache blowup -> batch amplification -> tail latency. Mitigations applied: global draft TTL=30s, eviction=aggressive, spec-dec concurrency reduced, ingress throttles on affected routes.
casey_oncall: Handoff summary: please keep throttle until 95p latency < 1.2s for 30m. Track KV insert_rate and batch_size. If insert_rate > baseline*2, re-escalate.
jordan_r: opening rollback PR for key-prefix change. Link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/kv/PR/4321 (do not merge until staging verified).
devex-liz: creating regression test ticket: https://issues.internal/RED-9273 — test ensures speculative draft TTL cannot be omitted and key-prefix compatibility tests.
eli_support: customer comms: EOD update to affected customers sent. Saved drafts for those requests may be lost due to eviction; notified customers.
casey_oncall: next steps for postmortem: list all commits in deploy window, timeline of metrics, decision log for TTL values, and an action to add a deploy blocker for config that can unset TTLs.
maria_g: attaching quick logs snippet for the incident:
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] kvcache.insert key=spec:draft:abc123 size=24kb ttl=3600
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] kvcache.insert key=spec:draft:def456 size=21kb ttl=3600
[2026-03-15T14:03:05Z] batch.size worker=12 size=46
[2026-03-15T14:04:29Z] mem.used node=gpux-7 pct=88.3
```
casey_oncall: OK handing off to @jordan_r in 20m. escalate if anything spikes. tagging this thread as incident-high and creating a postmortem template. :white_check_mark:
jordan_r: ack, I'll take over. leaving a note: do not merge PR 4321 until staging signoff.
incident-bot: Incident severity set to P2. Postmortem assigned to maria_g, due in 72h.
casey_oncall: thanks team. ongoing monitoring, will join if anything changes.
